patterns.upstream_heading: Inflated claims about importance and legacy
patterns.rationale: Importance and legacy language requires article-level editorial judgment.
Named entities may be necessary proof, product, or source references.
Participial phrasing is valid when it carries real causal meaning.

exceptions: Approved, source-supported commercial language remains proof governed.
patterns.rationale: Existing unsupported-hype rules block the deterministic subset; other sales language remains contextual.

exceptions: A visible authoritative citation may supply the attribution.
patterns.rationale: Existing proof and source-support guards own attribution decisions.
Challenges and outlook sections can be useful when the brief calls for them.

exceptions: Necessary AI product terminology remains allowed when vault aligned.
patterns.rationale: Existing AI-phrase rules block the deterministic subset; remaining vocabulary is contextual.
Copular alternatives are sometimes the clearest wording.

patterns.upstream_heading: Not X but Y and clipped negative endings
exceptions: Valid comparisons and FAQ answers remain allowed outside the exact blocked construction.
patterns.rationale: The existing not-just-but-also rule blocks the deterministic subset; clipped endings remain advisory.
Groups of three may be deliberate Simpro signature language.

patterns.upstream_heading: Changing names and repeating sentence openings
patterns.rationale: The existing three-repeat detector blocks formulaic openings; deliberate repetition and naming stay advisory.

patterns.upstream_heading: False from X to Y ranges
patterns.rationale: Ranges require semantic review because real scope and date ranges are valid.

exceptions: FAQ question headings retain the existing carve-out.
patterns.rationale: The existing passive-voice detector remains narrow; technical and evidence-led passive voice may be valid.

exceptions: En dashes in ranges and exact source titles remain allowed.
Double hyphens are not imported as a new ban.
patterns.rationale: Simpro blocks em dashes. En dashes and double hyphens are not imported as Humanizer bans.
Bold use depends on section structure and reader scanning needs.
Bold mini-headings can be useful in concise operational lists.

exceptions: Proper nouns and quoted titles retain existing handling.
patterns.rationale: The existing heading capitalization rule covers the deterministic Simpro subset.
Emoji suitability depends on channel and article treatment.

exceptions: Never normalize or rewrite exact approved quotations.
patterns.rationale: Exact quotation integrity outranks upstream quote-style conversion.

patterns.upstream_heading: Chatbot text left in the answer
patterns.rationale: Leaked assistant residue has no legitimate public-blog use.

enforcement.pattern: \b(?:i hope this helps|hope this helps|let me know|would you like me to|want me to(?: give examples)?|should i continue|you(?:'|’)re absolutely right|as an ai(?: language model)?|feel free to ask)\b
enforcement.message: Remove chatbot residue from public blog copy.
enforcement.suggestion: Delete the assistant-facing phrase and end with the article’s intended reader action.

exceptions: Legal, safety, correction, and scope limitations remain valid.
patterns.rationale: Unsupported factual guesses remain proof-gated; legitimate limitations remain allowed.

exceptions: Excluded because it targets assistant replies rather than blog prose.
patterns.rationale: Assistant agreeability guidance does not apply to finished blog prose.

exceptions: Only the existing exact blocker phrases are enforced.
patterns.rationale: Existing filler and setup rules block the deterministic subset; additional phrases remain advisory.
Qualifiers can accurately communicate evidence and product boundaries.
Endings require article-level judgment about the promised payoff.
Hyphenated technical terms and compounds are often correct.

patterns.upstream_heading: Pretending to reveal a deeper truth
patterns.rationale: Deeper-truth framing may be valid author opinion when clearly framed.

exceptions: Only the existing exact blocker phrases are enforced.
patterns.rationale: Existing setup rules block deterministic announcements; other transitions remain advisory.

patterns.upstream_heading: A heading repeated in the first sentence
patterns.rationale: A heading echo can provide a direct answer and is not automatically redundant.

exceptions: Excluded for blogs because change-history wording can be necessary.
patterns.rationale: Previous-version wording is valid in update, migration, and comparison content.
Named-author blogs may use short punchlines and deliberate fragments.
A saying may be authentic when it fits the author and subject.
Named-author blogs may use candid first-person judgment when genuine.

exceptions: FAQs and evidence-backed buyer objections are allowed.
patterns.rationale: Real buyer objections and FAQ answers remain valid.
Real evaluated alternatives remain valid in comparison content.
